title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous page. S is a normal base with function field K. X/S is a smooth proper curve, and T ⊂ X is a divisor finite étale over S, made of sections g_i. U = X − T, considered with tame ramification along T. Write π_1 (or π) for the geometric (tame) fundamental group π_1(U_{K̄}). There are two extensions: E_U of the arithmetic fundamental group of S by π, and E_{U_K} of E_K = Gal(K̄/K) by π. A K-rational point f_K of U_K gives a section of E_{U_K} → E_K. At a codimension-one point s of S, the point f specializes into the boundary, f(s) = g_i(s); D is the reduced closure of this locus. The previous page showed that the inertia group I_{s'} ⊂ E_K at a point s' of K̄ over s is sent, by the composite E_K → E_{U_K} → E_U, into π_1 and in fact into the cusp (loop) subgroup L_i.

This page localizes at s. N_{s'} is the decomposition group at s'. Geometrically it is π_1 of the 'punctured disk' around the germ of D at s. The sub-extension of N_{s'} by π inside E_{U_K} inherits a section from the section defined by f_K. The geometric interpretation is as follows.
- Õ_s is the (non-strict) henselization of the DVR O_{S,s}, a henselian trait. S̃ = Spec Õ_s, and K̃ is its fraction field.
- (23): N_{s'} ≅ E_{K̃} = Gal(K̄/K̃). This is the standard identification of a decomposition group with the absolute Galois group of the henselization.
- (24): the induced sub-extension is 1 → π → E_{U_{K̃}} = π_1(U_{K̃}) → E_{K̃} → 1.
- (25): it maps, by specialization over the henselian trait, to 1 → π → E_{U_{S̃}} → E_{Õ} ≅ Gal(k̄/k) → 1, with k = k(s).

The next page assembles this into a 3×3 diagram. The kernel of E_{U_{K̃}} → E_{U_{Õ}} maps isomorphically onto the inertia I_{s'} ≅ T, the tame inertia Ẑ'(1). The section from f_{K̃}, composed down, sends T into π via K_i∘(μ, id_T), where K_i is the loop homomorphism at the cusp i and μ is an intersection multiplicity. So the decomposition group normalizes the cusp subgroup L_i = K_i(T) in E_{U_{Õ}}.

Purpose: understand how sections coming from rational points behave locally at places where the point runs into a cusp. This is the local, 'cuspidal' behaviour of sections in the section-conjecture circle of ideas from the Longue Marche period.
errors: The identification of π on both rows of (24)/(25) (π_1(U_{K̄}) ≅ π_1(U_{k̄})) only holds for tame or prime-to-p fundamental groups when char k > 0. This is presumably intended, since tame ramification was assumed on the previous page, but it is not restated here.

Minor terminology: N_{s'} is called 'groupe d'inertie' in the transcription, while the previous page calls it the decomposition group. Mathematically (23) is correct only for the decomposition group, and the image likely reads 'décomposition'.
The notation is not uniform: (25) writes E_U, but the next page writes E_{U_Õ}; U here means U restricted to S̃.

ideas.what: Decomposition group at a codimension-one point identified with the Galois group of the fraction field of the (non-strict) henselization; geometrically, π_1 of the punctured tubular neighbourhood of the divisor germ.
ideas.modern_name: decomposition group = Gal(K̄/K^h); 'punctured disk' fundamental group
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Hilbert decomposition theory; henselization, Nagata/Grothendieck EGA IV)

ideas.what: Restricting the fundamental extension of a hyperbolic curve to a local decomposition group, and specializing via the tame specialization map over a henselian trait (exact rows over Gal(K̃) and Gal(k)).
ideas.modern_name: specialization of tame fundamental groups over a henselian DVR; local fundamental extension

ideas.what: A rational point that reduces to a cusp at a place gives a local section whose restriction to inertia factors through the cusp loop subgroup, scaled by the intersection multiplicity μ. Hence the decomposition group lands in the normalizer of the cuspidal subgroup L_i.
ideas.modern_name: cuspidal behaviour of sections / packets of cuspidal sections; local reduction of sections to cusps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983, sections 'at infinity'); developed by Nakamura, Hoshi, Stix and others
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983) mentions cuspidal sections; the detailed local computation is unsure

missed.claim: A detailed manuscript working-out of how sections from rational points behave over a higher-dimensional base S. At a codimension-one place where the point meets the boundary T, the induced local section on the henselized trait sends tame inertia into a cusp subgroup via μ times the loop homomorphism. This is essentially what later appears in the literature on cuspidal sections (Nakamura, Stix's book). It is of historical rather than mathematical novelty.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck had worked out the local, cuspidal side of the section conjecture in families. This is relevant to crediting the origins of cuspidal-section theory, but it contains no new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: This page is a standard localization: decomposition group equals the Galois group of the henselization, plus tame specialization over a henselian trait. It sets up the known fact that points meeting cusps yield sections normalizing cusp subgroups. The material is historically interesting as early detail around the section conjecture, but it is mathematically routine and largely present in later literature.
transcription_corrections: '(groupe d'inertie de E_{K,K̄} en s')' should most likely read '(groupe de décomposition de E_{K,K̄} en s')', consistent with the previous page and with (23).
The marginal insertion near line 3 appears to be a struck-through 'E_{U_{K̃}} ...', with an indication like 'l'extension ... de'. It is largely crossed out.
'Lien' / 'L'interprétation géométrique de ces construc- considérer d'autre part leur semblable de' is crossed out. The surviving text reads '...tions provient de la suivante'.
